boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named, campus-based UCF study environments with documented quiet, collaborative, computer, or reservable-work features.

cards.title: Set up beneath the vaulted ceiling
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Bring a reading-heavy task and choose a seat facing the campus view; the room has 235 seats and natural light.
cards.short_summary: A large, quiet reading room with high ceilings and broad campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries describes Room 405 as a quiet fourth-floor study space with 235 seats, vaulted ceilings, and a 270-degree campus view.
cards.access_notes: Located in the John C. Hitt Library; check library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Use the no-talk zone for deep focus
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Silence your phone before settling in and save collaborative work for another room; this 131-seat space prohibits talking.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent room for uninterrupted individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries states that Silent Study, Room 450, has 131 seats and requires silenced phones with no talking.
cards.access_notes: Located in the John C. Hitt Library; follow the no-talking rule and check library access and hours.

cards.title: Build a work session around a desktop
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, second floor main level
cards.notes: Choose this open commons when you need a desktop, accessible power, portable whiteboard, or flexible group seating.
cards.short_summary: A large technology-rich commons for individual or collaborative coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries lists the Knowledge Commons as a 24,800-square-foot learning and technology environment with 196 desktop PCs, power-accessible seating, varied seating, and portable whiteboards.
cards.source_title: John C. Hitt Library - UCF Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the library's second-floor main level; check library access and hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: John C. Hitt Library First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve a ground-floor project room
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, first floor
cards.notes: Book ahead for course-related group work, then check in within 15 minutes using the confirmation link or room QR code.
cards.short_summary: Reservable first-floor rooms for structured group study.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries lists study rooms on the John C. Hitt Library first floor and says eligible UCF users may reserve rooms up to four hours per day.
cards.access_notes: For currently enrolled UCF students, faculty, and staff; reserve up to three days ahead and check in within 15 minutes.

cards.entity_name: John C. Hitt Library Third-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Plan a small group session upstairs
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, third floor
cards.notes: Use a reservable room for course work, and leave promptly if another patron has a reservation for the unlocked space.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor reservable rooms suited to focused group coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries lists multiple third-floor John C. Hitt Library study rooms and states that unreserved users may be asked to leave when a reservation begins.
cards.access_notes: For currently enrolled UCF students, faculty, and staff; rooms are unlocked but require a reservation when claimed.

cards.entity_name: John C. Hitt Library Fourth-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Book a fourth-floor room near quiet study
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Reserve before you arrive for group coursework; selected rooms include motion-activated door openers for easier access.
cards.short_summary: Reservable fourth-floor study rooms alongside the library's quiet-study level.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries lists fourth-floor study rooms and identifies rooms 459, 461, and 469 as having motion-activated door openers.
cards.access_notes: For currently enrolled UCF students, faculty, and staff; use the library reservation system and observe room occupancy limits.

cards.title: Gather a larger team in Suite 360
cards.subtitle: John C. Hitt Library, third floor
cards.notes: Choose this option for a larger group and reserve through LibCal; each conference room seats up to 12 people.
cards.short_summary: Two bookable third-floor conference rooms for larger study teams.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Libraries says two Suite 360 Conference Rooms on the third floor seat up to 12 people and are bookable through LibCal.
cards.access_notes: Available for booking via LibCal; confirm availability and applicable library booking rules before going.

cards.entity_name: Technology Commons I Group Study Spaces
cards.title: Pair group work with a computer lab
cards.subtitle: Technology Commons I, main campus
cards.notes: Head here when your group needs campus computers or device support; the commons also provides laptop and tablet checkout.
cards.short_summary: Group-study space within UCF's technology commons network.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Academic Advocacy states that Technology Commons offers large computer labs, laptop and tablet checkout, and group study spaces in Technology Commons I.
cards.access_notes: Check Technology Commons operations and equipment-loan requirements before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Technology Commons II Group Study Spaces
cards.title: Work beside campus tech support
cards.subtitle: Technology Commons II, main campus
cards.notes: Use this campus computer-lab setting for a group work block, and contact the Student Support Desk if a device problem comes up.
cards.short_summary: A group-work option connected to UCF computer labs and support.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Academic Advocacy identifies Technology Commons II as one of the locations with large computer labs, group study spaces, and access to the Student Support Desk.
cards.access_notes: Check Technology Commons operations and equipment-loan requirements before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Classroom Building I, Room 101 Group Study Space
cards.title: Make Room 101 your tech-enabled meeting point
cards.subtitle: Classroom Building I, Room 101, main campus
cards.notes: Use this named group-study location when you need a computer-lab environment; ask the Student Support Desk for device assistance.
cards.short_summary: A specifically identified group-study location within Classroom Building I.
cards.evidence_claim: UCF Academic Advocacy lists Classroom Building I, Room 101 among Technology Commons locations offering large computer labs and group study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Check Technology Commons operations and room availability before visiting.
